Claire —

Thanks for the diagrams, they helped a lot. High-level answers inline below; I'll follow up with a short handoff doc before Friday's review. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

- Control plane tenant admission: the recommended pattern is to keep admission decisions in Redwood's private controlplane (Control API). That gives us the ability to enforce per-tenant quotas and rollout policies centrally while keeping the dataplane local. For OrchardCloud's model, we suggest "Control API + local admission cache" so the edge pod can make fast acceptance decisions when the controlplane is unreachable.

- Sidecar vs shared egress proxy: sidecar offers stronger tenant isolation and a simpler KV cache locality model, but adds per-pod overhead. Shared egress proxy is cheaper but requires careful connection pooling. Recommended defaults: MTU 1400 for encapsulated overlay (we've seen fragmentation at 1500 in a few colo fabrics), gRPC keepalive 120s server-side, 30s client-side, and a token refresh jitter of 10%. These settings reduce mid-stream KV cache resets for sequence lengths >1k.

- Hosted fallback: yes, we support transparent fallback to a trimmed model variant in the hosted tier. That must be pre-authorized in the rollout policy and listed in the canary/rollback config. We'll need a signed SLA appendix if OrchardCloud expects automatic model fallthrough during capacity events.

Action items:
1) Jonas to produce a short runbook snippet on local admission cache behavior (image + conditions).
2) Karthik to validate MTU/keepalive defaults against your colo fabric and report back.
3) Naomi to draft the SLA appendix language for model fallback.

I'll attach the two-line runbook snippet and a protocol matrix by EOD.

- Naomi

Naomi / Claire —

I've sketched the runbook snippet and attached it to this thread (copied below). Main operational notes: 

1) Local admission cache behavior:
- Cache TTL: 45s
- Stale handling: fallback to last-known-good for up to 3 consecutive requests, then fall into degraded mode (accept limited request types).
- Telemetry: emit per-tenant admission_decision events with reason codes (RATE_LIMIT, QUOTA, UNKNOWN, LOCAL_CACHE_HIT).

2) KV cache resiliency patterns:
- Prefer sidecar for tenants with >50 qps sustained inference traffic. Shared proxy OK for bursty low-qps tenants.
- If using shared proxy, set connection pool min_conns=8 and per-connection max_requests=500 to avoid head-of-line stalls.

3) MTU/keepalive verification: Karthik, can you confirm whether your colo's overlay performs PMTU and will tolerate 1400? If not, we can move to 1360 as a safe default and document the perf delta.

I've included a one-paragraph example for the SLA appendix below — Naomi, please edit for legal tone.

--- runbook snippet ---
Runbook: local admission cache and degraded fallback
- Trigger: controlplane heartbeats miss 3x (3s interval)
- Behavior: local admission cache consulted for decision; if cache age > 45s, restrict model selection to pre-approved fallbacks and emit AdmissionFallback event.
- Recovery: when heartbeats resume, allow 10s window to stabilize before resuming normal rollout policy.
--- end snippet ---
